column1: # 1.0.2 only. Everything below is bound to this update's main build ID: the three CUTS in patches.py, the UE_CVAR offsets the rewriter writes into
# main.fixups.tsv, and the shader tables (the two .ushaderbytecode archives change with an update). A base-only 1.0.1 dump has a different build ID and
# must be registered as its own build row rather than reusing these tables.

# Unreal: nninitStartup reserves a 62 GB address region and its FMallocBinned3 takes 37 GB of it, so a 64 GB alias region for the bring-up on the Mac. The rewriter cuts the allocator in any Unreal 4 / 5 main (dm/tools/ue_malloc.py) and gives the region what the alias region has room for (dm/tools/ue_region.py), so an iPhone takes a smaller guest block, as Octopath Traveler 0's profile (docs/reference/memory.md)
# the NPDM declares 20 MB of system resource
# 60 fps: the game sets present interval 1 and then 2 (30 fps) itself, which it applies again on level loads. At 30 fps a frame's budget is 33.33 ms and the measured frame time
# is 33.4-33.8 ms, so every frame misses the budget a little and one is dropped now and then (19 of 300 frames, p99 66.67 ms -- the hitch on camera cuts); rendering costs 5.4 ms
# of GPU and 1.6 ms of CPU, so 60 fps has room. It also fixes the sound running ahead of the picture: audio keeps real time, and a frame time 1.2% over budget made the picture
# fall behind it by about 0.7 s a minute. At 60 fps: frame time p50 16.69 ms, 0 frames dropped of 300, p99 16.67 ms
# the game sets near = 0 via nvnDeviceSetDepthMode (log: the bundled pipeline archive was made for
# depth near=-w and rejected), so the offline builds must use main0_z (docs/reference/shaders.md)
# the vertex shaders of 27 materials pick a texture slot at run time (log: "[RED] shader ... reflection conversion failed: a texture handle the translator could not
# trace to one slot (profile key tex_dyn_slots off)", then "failed to load" and the draw is skipped): the same shape as FINAL FANTASY RESONANCE and OCTOPATH TRAVELER 0
# the decoded shader code archives: the engine's global shaders and the game's material shaders
